source_caption:
🎬 Two Weeks Notice (2002)

Two Weeks Notice follows Lucy Kelson, a brilliant and dedicated environmental lawyer who accepts a job working for George Wade, a charming but irresponsible billionaire real estate developer in New York City. Although Lucy initially hopes to use her position to protect historic buildings and support important community causes, she quickly discovers that George depends on her for almost every decision in his life. From complicated business matters and personal relationships to choosing his clothes and handling everyday problems, Lucy finds herself constantly managing George’s chaotic lifestyle. Frustrated by his demanding behavior and lack of independence, she finally decides to resign and gives him two weeks’ notice. However, as George searches for her replacement, both begin to realize that their relationship has become more meaningful than either expected. Through hilarious misunderstandings, romantic complications, and unexpected emotional moments, the two discover that love can develop in the most unlikely circumstances. Combining charming comedy, heartfelt romance, and entertaining workplace situations, the film explores love, ambition, independence, friendship, and the importance of appreciating the people closest to us.

🎭 Genre: Romantic Comedy • Romance • Comedy

⭐ IMDb: 6.2/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 41m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Marc Lawrence

🏆 Recognition: Starring Sandra Bullock, Hugh Grant, Alicia Witt, and Dana Ivey, the film became a commercial success, earning approximately $199 million worldwide. Known for the entertaining chemistry between Bullock and Grant, its witty dialogue, and memorable romantic moments, it remains a recognizable early-2000s romantic comedy.

source_details.synopsis: Two Weeks Notice is a 2002 American romantic comedy film written and directed by Marc Lawrence and starring Sandra Bullock and Hugh Grant, with Alicia Witt, Dana Ivey, Robert Klein, and Heather Burns in supporting roles. In the film, an idealistic, liberal lawyer (Bullock) goes to work for a narcissistic, billionaire developer (Grant) and they form an unlikely pair. The film was released in the United States on December 20, 2002, by Warner Bros. Pictures. It received mixed reviews from critics and grossed $199 million worldwide.
